parts.text: The HARE (Human-AI REsearch) group (led by John Chen) at the University of Arizona College of Information Science is looking for a postdoctoral researcher to join our

on advancing qualitative research through human-AI collaboration. The project is in collaboration with Northwestern University (Co-PIs: Uri Wilensky, Michael Horn).

The postdoc will have opportunities to:
Study qualitative researchers perspectives and current practices about AI Conduct interviews and co-design sessions with qualitative researchers about human-AI interfaces Collaborate with qualitative researchers across institutions and disciplines Lead publications in top-tier venues Pursue their own research and professional development

We’re especially interested in candidates with (or expected by early 2027) a PhD in HCI, computer science, learning sciences, or a related field, with substantial experience in qualitative research and co-design/participatory design methods.

While experiences with machine learning or natural language processing is a plus, we DO NOT require you to have deep expertise around that. Instead, we want you to be open-minded and interested in exploring this direction.

Note for international applicants: the position IS open to visa holders with F1/OPT, J1, or other existing employment authorization. At this point, our college does not sponsor H1-B for postdoc scholars.

Send your application through:

The University of Arizona College of Information Science focuses on the intersection of people, data, and technology, offering innovative programs in information science, data science, cybersecurity, game design, and immersive technologies. Established in 2023 and expanded in 2025, the college provides STEM-designated undergraduate and master’s degrees, and a PhD. in Information. With nationally ranked programs such as the #1 Best Online Bachelor’s in Cybersecurity, #4 Best Master’s in Data Science, and #10 Global Ranking of Library an Information Science Programs, we emphasize computational thinking, ethical reasoning, and multicultural communication while driving research and partnerships such as Arizona Cybersecurity Academy, AI Core, Gaming and Virtual Worlds, Human -Centered Computing, and many other areas of research.
